A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CARVE research, with matching authors, title, algorithm, and original experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, CARVE evaluations on four benchmarks, comparisons with other methods, and hyperparameter and prompt experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, component ablations, statistical analyses, resource measurements, newer-model experiments, and a failure case.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same general/task-specific attention extraction, regularized attention ratio, weighted fusion, top-p thresholding, top-K connected-region selection, masking, cropping, resizing, and final inference. Additive contrast and internal attention modification are experimental alternatives, not revisions to CARVE. Appendix I explicitly applies the unchanged pipeline to newer models.

E1.justification: v3 retains A-OKVQA, POPE, V*, and TextVQA and adds evaluated document understanding, chart comprehension, and science-question reasoning through DocVQA, ChartQA, and ScienceQA (Table 3). Appendix J additionally examines a BLINK relative-depth failure case; this is a single case, not a full BLINK benchmark evaluation.

E2.justification: SD-RPN is newly evaluated alongside ViCrop and CARVE in v3 Table 3, adding a trained region-selection comparator. The existing SAM, YOLO, CLIP, and three ViCrop variants remain in the corresponding TextVQA comparison, moved from v1 Table 3 to v3 Table 5. The comparator membership change is limited.

E3.justification: New protocols include sampled DocVQA validation data, ChartQA and image-containing ScienceQA test sets, EM/ANLS/relaxed/multiple-choice metrics, component controls, temperature variation, and resource measurements over 100 ChartQA samples. Appendix I adds Qwen3-VL-2B/4B and Gemma-3-27B-it configurations. The retained external-tool timing comparison is relabeled from GPU time to end-to-end inference latency with unchanged values; this is a reported metric revision, not evidence that those measurements were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls testing direct question-attention masking and internal attention modification (Table 4), multiplicative versus additive contrast and attention uniformity (Appendix G), decoding-temperature robustness (Appendix B.3), measured inference overhead, and a BLINK depth-reasoning failure analysis. These substantially expand investigation of mechanism, robustness, and failure conditions beyond v1's retained time-step, layer, masking, and prompt studies.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix H adds V* bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples and paired McNemar tests for all four original models. Table 11 adds means and standard deviations for attention-uniformity measurements over 500 images, and Appendix B.1 specifies a DocVQA sampling seed. The existing Figure 5 confidence intervals and ten-trial prompt study remain; their presence is not new.

E6.justification: Substantial new benchmark, ablation, newer-model, timing, memory, and failure-case results are reported. Existing values also change: Table 1's LLaVA-1.5-13B Tfull scores move from 76.5 to 76.9 on A-OKVQA and 70.0 to 70.2 on V*. Table 2 changes Qwen2.5-VL-3B's [20,25] V* score from 57.1 to 56.5 and LLaVA-1.5-7B's corresponding TextVQA score from 58.2 to 57.9. These are reported numerical revisions, not established performance gains from a changed method.

T1.justification: The decomposition becomes an explicit modeling assumption, and Appendix C qualifies uniqueness and the retained results as properties of an idealized model. v1's approximation-error bound, optimal-regularization proposition, and entropy-monotonicity theorem in C.4–C.6 are removed. Convexity and closed-form derivations remain. The computational analysis is retained with corrected numerical examples, including combined speedup changing from 1.24 to 1.19.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the central theoretical contribution from a claimed proof of signal/noise decomposition to approximate separation under a multiplicative assumption. The abstract also replaces the headline 'up to 75%' improvement with a seven-benchmark claim focused on visual perception and recent as well as earlier models. CARVE's training-free contribution and attention-complexity observations remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains gains in terms of perceptual task demands, scale normalization, and model capability. Its main-text limitations and Appendix J identify loss of global spatial context, demonstrate a depth-ordering failure, acknowledge nonlinear attention interactions and imperfect uniformity, and discuss the accuracy–inference-cost tradeoff. These materially qualify applicability beyond v1's discussion of excessive masking.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code link, specifies lambda=0.05, documents extended dataset splits and sample counts, attention-fusion settings, mask parameters, scoring procedures, and resource-measurement conditions. Hardware reporting expands from four RTX A6000 GPUs to an A6000/H20 allocation. These are substantial documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish that newly disclosed settings changed existing experiments or verify the linked code's availability.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused toward visual-token processing, attention-head methods, and trained grounding/zooming systems, adding discussion of CogCoM, CogAgent, Ferret-UI, and visual-explanation methods. v3 explicitly credits ViCrop as inspiration and introduces SD-RPN positioning. Earlier discussion and references concerning RECIPE, DistiLLM-2, BLIP-2, and other works are removed; retained works' publication updates are not counted as new research.

P1.justification: v3 extensively condenses and rewrites retained introduction, related-work, attention-analysis, and results passages. Section 3 and its subsections receive clearer descriptive titles, 'Method Analysis' becomes 'Experiments,' and implementation, validation, statistics, and limitations receive expanded organization. This exceeds the structural changes attributable solely to added experiments.

P2.justification: The paper adopts substantially different typography, margins, headers, float placement, and table styling. Existing results tables replace green highlighting and parenthesized gains with bold/underlined rankings and superscript gains. Numerous new tables and two new case-study figures are added. The original prompt table and masking visualizations are retained and renumbered, not replaced.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important evidential gap: new component and additive-contrast controls directly test CARVE's central design choices, while V* significance analyses support the large gains on a small benchmark. Broader evaluations, measured overhead, and a concrete failure case improve assessment of applicability and practical cost. Explicit theoretical assumptions and removal of overstated results also improve claim calibration. The decomposition remains an idealized model, but the paper now provides substantially stronger empirical support and clearer boundaries.
